answer: We formulate a dynamic opportunity-cost bond mechanism alongside a subgame-perfect slashing matrix bound by zero-knowledge verifiable delay primitives. If a malicious actor attempts to forge k virtual identities, the superlinear staking collateral requirement and deterministic slash penalty yield a strictly negative expected payoff E[Π_attack] < 0. Furthermore, the non-trivial null space kernel of the penalty tensor ensures that maintaining a single honest consensus thread represents the unique subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium.
